question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` allow scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what exact grammar is acceptable for Gateway browser-origin authorization?
rationale: The request changes which browser origins may reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket authorization paths, and current docs/config only define full-origin allowlisting plus the global `*` escape hatch.

options.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
options.body: Define a small grammar, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allowed/rejected cases before accepting the feature.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` for intentionally broad local testing.

options.title: Fold into broader origin-pattern design
options.body: Wait for the loopback pattern work to settle, then decide whether extension scheme wildcards belong in that same contract.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
recommendation.body: Define a small grammar, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allowed/rejected cases before accepting the feature.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and hardened the central Gateway origin-check boundary and merged the current global wildcard behavior.
